stem.text: A ball is set in motion at P on a frictionless surface. It moves up slope PQ, along the horizontal surface QR and finally descends slope RS.

stem.alt: Track with points P, Q, R and S; a ball on the rising slope PQ with an arrow showing its direction of motion; horizontal section QR; falling slope RS.

stem.text: Which graph could represent the variation with time $t$ of the ball's speed $v$ as the ball moves from P to S?

A.alt: Graph with vertical axis v and horizontal axis t, origin 0. A line falls from a point on the v-axis, becomes horizontal, then rises steeply.

B.alt: Graph with vertical axis v and horizontal axis t, origin 0. A line falls, then falls more gently, then rises steeply.

C.alt: Graph with vertical axis v and horizontal axis t, origin 0. A line falls from a point on the v-axis, becomes horizontal, then rises steeply.

D.alt: Graph with vertical axis v and horizontal axis t, origin 0. A curve rises from the origin with decreasing slope, then rises steeply near the end.
